    Item locations at a response probability

    ess_locations.Rd

    Converts IRT item parameters into ESS item locations. The location of a dichotomous item is the ability at which an examinee answers it correctly with probability `rp`. A polytomous item with maximum score K gives K locations ("pages"), one for each score point k = 1, ..., K: the ability at which an examinee earns score k or higher with probability `rp`.

    Usage

    ess_locations(
  pars,
  model = NULL,
  rp = 0.67,
  D = 1,
  item = 1,
  a = "a",
  b = "b",
  c = "c",
  guessing = c("none", "rescale", "huynh"),
  slope = 1,
  intercept = 0,
  sep = "_"
)

    Arguments

    pars

    A data frame of item parameters, one row per item.

    model

    The IRT model: `"rasch"`, `"2pl"`, `"3pl"` (dichotomous) or `"pcm"`, `"gpcm"`, `"grm"` (polytomous). Either one value for every item or one value per row of `pars`, which allows mixed-format tests. If `NULL`, `pars` must have a column named `model`.

    rp

    Response probability, between 0 and 1. The default 0.67 is the usual RP67; 0.5 returns the RP50 location (`b` for Rasch and 2PL items).

    D

    Scaling constant: 1 for the logistic metric (mirt, flexMIRT, Winsteps), 1.702 (or 1.7) for the normal metric (PARSCALE, BILOG-MG and many operational programs).

    item

    Column of `pars` holding the item ID, by name or position.

    a

    Column holding the discrimination (slope). Not used for `"rasch"` and `"pcm"` items, where it is fixed at 1.

    b

    Threshold columns. Either a prefix (the default `"b"` matches columns `b`, `b1`, `b2`, ...; a column `b` counts as `b1`) or a character vector naming the threshold columns in order. Dichotomous items use one threshold; polytomous items use thresholds 1 to K and `NA` after that, so items with different maximum scores can share one table. See Details for what the thresholds mean under each model.

    c

    Column holding the lower asymptote (pseudo-guessing) of `"3pl"` items.

    guessing

    How `rp` is applied to `"3pl"` items: * `"none"` (default): P(correct) = `rp`. Requires `rp > c`. * `"rescale"`: P(correct) = c + (1 - c) `rp`, i.e. `rp` of the way from the guessing floor to 1. * `"huynh"`: P(correct) = (2 + c) / 3 (Huynh, 1998, 2006). `rp` is not used for these items; with c = 0 this is 2/3.

    Other models are not affected.

    slope, intercept

    Linear transformation to a reporting scale: `location = intercept + slope * theta`. `slope` must be positive so that item order is kept.

    sep

    Separator between item ID and score point in the `Item_ID` of a polytomous score point (`"Q12_2"`).

    Value

    A data frame with one row per location: `Item_ID` (the item ID for dichotomous items, item ID, `sep` and score point for polytomous items), `item`, `score`, `max_score`, `model`, `p` (the probability the location was solved for), `theta` and `location` (`theta` on the reporting scale). Rows keep the order of `pars`; they are not sorted by location.

    Details

    **Dichotomous items.** With P(theta) = c + (1 - c) / (1 + exp(-D a (theta - b))), the location is `theta = b + log((p - c) / (1 - p)) / (D a)`, where p is the target probability (`rp`, or as set by `guessing`). Rasch items have a = 1 and c = 0; 2PL items have c = 0. Under Rasch, changing `rp` moves every item by the same amount, so item order does not change. Under 2PL and 3PL the shift is `1 / (D a)` times larger for less discriminating items, so `rp` can change item order.

    **Polytomous items.** The location of score point k solves P(X >= k | theta) = `rp`. These locations are always increasing in k within an item. * `"grm"`: the thresholds are the category boundaries `b_k` of P(X >= k) = 1 / (1 + exp(-D a (theta - b_k))), so `theta_k = b_k + log(rp / (1 - rp)) / (D a)`. Boundaries must increase. * `"pcm"`, `"gpcm"`: the thresholds are step difficulties `delta_v` of P(X = k) proportional to exp(sum over v <= k of D a (theta - delta_v)). They may be disordered. The location is found numerically.

    Parameterizations differ between programs; convert before calling. For mirt, `"graded"` items give `b_k = -d_k / a`, and `"gpcm"` items (with the default scoring 0, 1, ..., K) give `delta_k = -(d_k - d_(k-1)) / a`. Programs that report an item location b with step deviations d_v use `delta_v = b - d_v` (PARSCALE) or `b + d_v`, depending on sign convention.

    References

    Huynh, H. (1998). On score locations of binary and partial credit items and their applications to item mapping and criterion-referenced interpretation. *Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics, 23*(1), 35-56.

    Huynh, H. (2006). A clarification on the response probability criterion RP67 for standard settings based on bookmark and item mapping. *Educational Measurement: Issues and Practice, 25*(2), 19-20.

    Examples

    # Mixed-format test: 3PL multiple-choice items and a GPCM constructed-
# response item scored 0-3
pars <- data.frame(
  Item_ID = c("MC1", "MC2", "CR1"),
  model   = c("3pl", "3pl", "gpcm"),
  a  = c(1.2, 0.7, 0.9),
  b1 = c(-0.5, 0.3, -1.0),
  b2 = c(NA, NA, 0.2),
  b3 = c(NA, NA, 1.1),
  c  = c(0.20, 0.25, NA)
)
ess_locations(pars, D = 1.702)
#>   Item_ID item score max_score model    p      theta   location
#> 1     MC1  MC1     1         1   3pl 0.67 -0.3268507 -0.3268507
#> 2     MC2  MC2     1         1   3pl 0.67  0.5024191  0.5024191
#> 3   CR1_1  CR1     1         3  gpcm 0.67 -0.6939925 -0.6939925
#> 4   CR1_2  CR1     2         3  gpcm 0.67  0.5041366  0.5041366
#> 5   CR1_3  CR1     3         3  gpcm 0.67  1.6324590  1.6324590

# RP50 and Huynh's guessing-adjusted RP for the 3PL items
ess_locations(pars, rp = 0.5, D = 1.702)
#>   Item_ID item score max_score model   p      theta   location
#> 1     MC1  MC1     1         1   3pl 0.5 -0.7501105 -0.7501105
#> 2     MC2  MC2     1         1   3pl 0.5 -0.2817922 -0.2817922
#> 3   CR1_1  CR1     1         3  gpcm 0.5 -1.0878028 -1.0878028
#> 4   CR1_2  CR1     2         3  gpcm 0.5  0.1623984  0.1623984
#> 5   CR1_3  CR1     3         3  gpcm 0.5  1.2267645  1.2267645
ess_locations(pars, D = 1.702, guessing = "huynh")
#>   Item_ID item score max_score model         p      theta   location
#> 1     MC1  MC1     1         1   3pl 0.7333333 -0.1606212 -0.1606212
#> 2     MC2  MC2     1         1   3pl 0.7500000  0.8817922  0.8817922
#> 3   CR1_1  CR1     1         3  gpcm 0.6700000 -0.6939925 -0.6939925
#> 4   CR1_2  CR1     2         3  gpcm 0.6700000  0.5041366  0.5041366
#> 5   CR1_3  CR1     3         3  gpcm 0.6700000  1.6324590  1.6324590

# Locations on a reporting scale (scale score = 500 + 50 * theta)
ess_locations(pars, D = 1.702, slope = 50, intercept = 500)
#>   Item_ID item score max_score model    p      theta location
#> 1     MC1  MC1     1         1   3pl 0.67 -0.3268507 483.6575
#> 2     MC2  MC2     1         1   3pl 0.67  0.5024191 525.1210
#> 3   CR1_1  CR1     1         3  gpcm 0.67 -0.6939925 465.3004
#> 4   CR1_2  CR1     2         3  gpcm 0.67  0.5041366 525.2068
#> 5   CR1_3  CR1     3         3  gpcm 0.67  1.6324590 581.6230
